subject: Request: custom SLA exhibit & order form language
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@crescenthealth.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@crescenthealth.com, ben.torres@crescenthealth.com
Date: Tue, 28 Nov 2028 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: custom SLA exhibit & order form language

Hi Aditya —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. CrescentHealth is excited about Redwood but procurement has a couple of blocking asks before legal will sign the MSA: specifically a custom SLA exhibit (availability and latency commitments for the order form) and evidence we can reference in the SOW (telemetry/alerts/retention, SOC 2 mapping, and an incident escalation runbook).

High-level asks: 
- Availability: example target of 99.995% monthly uptime for the models we plan to use (we can negotiate the final number).
- Latency: p95 inference latency < 350ms for the GA text-generation route and p95 < 150ms for small embeddings on the dedicated pool.
- Fallback behavior: explicit order form language describing graceful degradation, regional failover, and credits for sustained degraded performance.
- Evidence: an attachments folder (or link) with SOC 2 sections, telemetry sample, and an ops runbook or on-call matrix.

I've attached our redlines to the MSA (CrescentHealth_MSA_Redlines_v1.docx) and would like Redwood to propose order form exhibit language and any evidence you can provide. Legal wants to see proposed language, an evidence matrix, and an implementation timeline (how long it will take to stand up any dedicated pool or routing guarantees if needed).

Can you route to your sales+legal team and share a proposed addendum and evidence pack by close of week? We may need a short sync with procurement + legal to resolve a couple of specific clauses.

Best,
Olivia
Director, Procurement
CrescentHealth

Attachments: CrescentHealth_MSA_Redlines_v1.docx

From: aditya.rao@redwood.ai <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 28 Nov 2028 12:07:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request: custom SLA exhibit & order form language

Kimberly / Jordan — forwarding CrescentHealth procurement's asks. Short summary and suggested next steps: 

Summary of asks: availability target (~99.995%), p95 latency targets for generation and embeddings, detailed fallback language + credits, and an evidence pack (SOC 2 mapping, telemetry samples, on-call/runbook). They attached their MSA redlines.

Suggested approach: 
1) Kimberly: can you draft a compact SLA addendum (1-2 pages) + redline against their MSA where relevant? Focus on: availability definition (what counts as downtime), regional failover mechanics, and the service credit schedule tied to monthly uptime.
2) Jordan: can you produce order form language that maps plan/sku to the SLA tier and a short pricing delta for a dedicated pool commit (they will likely ask for dedicated capacity to reach p95 targets)? If we need a capacity commit, state lead time (2-4 weeks) and estimated uplift.
3) Karthik: can you prepare an evidence matrix (attachment) that maps statements in the addendum to deliverables we can provide (SOC 2 section links, sample telemetry export, ops runbook snapshot)?

Timing: Crescent asked for something by EOW (Friday). If we can't meet all evidence immediately, propose an interim "evidence bundle" with timelines for items behind an integration or audit.

I've attached an initial skeleton addendum (initial-draft-sla-addendum.docx) with suggested fallbacks and a basic credit table — feel free to edit.

I'll offer a 30-minute sync with the Crescent team once we have a draft.

Thanks,
Aditya
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Attachments: initial-draft-sla-addendum.docx

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 29 Nov 2028 09:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: custom SLA exhibit & order form language

On Tue, Nov 28, 2028 at 12:07 PM aditya.rao@redwood.ai wrote:
> Kimberly / Jordan — forwarding CrescentHealth procurement's asks. Short summary and suggested next steps: 
> ...

Thanks for the summary, Aditya. I reviewed CrescentHealth_MSA_Redlines_v1.docx and their commercial asks. A few high-level notes before I redline: 

- Availability definition: we should keep the definition bounded (control plane vs inference plane; scheduled maintenance windows excluded). Propose a 99.99% baseline for hosted API and an elevated "Dedicated SLA" (99.995%) that requires a dedicated pool order form commitment (monthly commit).
- Credits: propose a capped credit table (% monthly bill) with clear measurement windows and an exclusion for customer-induced incidents and force majeure.
- Latency: avoid absolute language tied to single-region p95 unless they accept a dedicated pool and a model pin. Instead offer a p95 guidance in the addendum and include a guaranteed p95 only for the dedicated pool SKU (order form exhibits). For hosted tiers, provide EM guidance only.
- Evidence: we can provide a runbook snapshot, SOC 2 mapping (control IDs), and a sample telemetry export. Full incidents and audit logs can be made available under an NDA or via limited retention export.

I've attached: redwood-addedendum-redline.docx (compact SLA addendum with tracked changes), runbook-and-evidence-matrix.xlsx (maps requested evidence to artifacts), and a short note for the sales team about lead time for dedicated capacity.

I also added a recommended clause for graceful degradation and a fallback to a lower-cost model variant with automatic client notification; this reduces risk while giving Crescent the functional guarantees they care about.

Next: Aditya, propose we share the revised redline + evidence matrix with Crescent and request a 30-minute legal/procurement sync. Jordan — please confirm the uplift for a 3-month dedicated commit (estimated +20% to monthly hosting).

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-addedendum-redline.docx; runbook-and-evidence-matrix.xlsx

From: jordan.blake@redwood.ai <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Quick commercial note: 
- Dedicated pool uplift: +18% for a 3-month minimum commitment, +12% for 6+ months. Lead time to provision: ~14 business days after order form countersigned and payment instrument validated.
- If Crescent prefers host-level availability without a dedicated commit, we can offer a guidance SLA but will not guarantee p95 latency.

I've updated the attached orderform-exhibit draft that maps SKU -> SLA tier and includes a line item for "Dedicated Capacity Setup Fee" and a checkbox for "Regional Failover Enabled." Also added a short paragraph tying the service credits to the monthly invoice for easier procurement reconciliation.

Recommend: Share Kimberly's redline + the orderform-exhibit draft and ask for a 30-min legal/procurement call. I can join and cover commercial/lead time.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-orderform-exhibit-v1.pdf

Thanks for the clear ask and for the redlines. We reviewed and have prepared proposed language and supporting evidence. Attached: redwood-addedendum-redline.docx (compact SLA addendum with tracked changes), redwood-orderform-exhibit-v1.pdf (order form mapping SKU->SLA), and runbook-and-evidence-matrix.xlsx.

Key callouts: 
- We can commit to a Dedicated SLA (99.995% monthly uptime) only when Crescent signs the dedicated pool order form and accepts the provisioning lead time (14 business days) and uplift (+18% for 3-month commitment).

- Evidence bundle includes SOC 2 mapping and a sample telemetry export; items that require an NDA or extra retention will be delivered on a timeline in the evidence matrix.

Would Crescent be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow 9–11am PT? If that works, we'll send a calendar invite and a DocuSign bridge for the orderform-exhibit so procurement can review the pricing and lead times during the sync.

Best,
